messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details: 
- What the failing test does:
  - AliasedNamespaceIterationTest.testIterateJDOM() delegates to doTestIterate(DocumentContainer.MODEL_JDOM).
  - doTestIterate(model) creates a JXPathContext over IterateAliasedNS.xml, registers the namespace prefix “a” for URI “ns”, and asserts that iterating the XPath “/a:doc/a:elem” produces two pointers: “/a:doc[1]/a:elem[1]” and “/a:doc[1]/a:elem[2]”.
- The XML under test (from the issue description) looks like:
  <a:doc xmlns:a="ns">
    <a:elem/>
    <b:elem xmlns:b="ns"/>
  </a:doc>
  Both elements are in the same namespace URI (“ns”), but use different prefixes (“a” and “b”).

- Expected behavior:
  - XPath name tests are resolved by namespace URI, not by prefix. Therefore, with the context mapping “a” → “ns”, “/a:doc/a:elem” should match both children since both are in the “ns” namespace and have local name “elem”. The two pointers should be “/a:doc[1]/a:elem[1]” and “/a:doc[1]/a:elem[2]”. This is exactly what the test asserts.

- Observed behavior (from the bug report):
  - JXPathContext.iteratePointers() returns the first element twice and omits the second one when the second uses a different prefix for the same namespace URI. This failure manifests in the JDOM model (testIterateDOM likely passes, while testIterateJDOM fails), meaning the problem is specific to the JDOM bridge.

- Root cause in the JDOM model:
  - The JDOM bridge selects children by constructing a JDOM Namespace from the context’s registered prefix and URI (e.g., Namespace.getNamespace("a", "ns")) and then querying children via Element.getChildren(localName, namespace).
  - In JDOM, Namespace equality includes both prefix and URI. So Element.getChildren("elem", Namespace("a","ns")) only returns children that actually use prefix “a”; it will not return “b:elem” even though it has the same URI.
  - As a result, only the “a:elem” child is found via that query. Due to the iterator/merging logic in the JDOM child iteration, the same “a:elem” child is produced twice while “b:elem” is missed entirely, matching the report: the first element is returned two times; the second is not returned.

- Why the DOM model doesn’t fail here:
  - The DOM model typically compares by namespace URI and local name directly, without relying on prefix-dependent constructs, so it correctly treats both children as equal by namespace and local name.

In short: The JDOM model in JXPath matches children using a JDOM Namespace object derived from the registered prefix, which couples prefix and URI. That makes matching depend on the element’s actual prefix instead of namespace URI. With multiple prefixes bound to the same URI, this causes elements with different prefixes to be skipped and can also lead to duplicate emission of a found child.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
